questions.title: Glaucoma drug class that reduces aqueous production
questions.question: Regarding the treatment of glaucoma, which one of the following groups of drugs reduces aqueous humour production?

explanations.A: Correct. Topical beta-blockers such as timolol block beta receptors on the ciliary epithelium, reducing the formation (production) of aqueous humour and thereby lowering intraocular pressure. Decreasing inflow, rather than increasing outflow, is their mechanism in glaucoma. This makes beta-blockers the aqueous-suppressing group here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Miotics (pilocarpine) lower pressure by INCREASING trabecular outflow through ciliary-muscle contraction, not by reducing production.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Prostaglandin analogues (latanoprost) lower pressure by increasing UVEOSCLERAL outflow, again an outflow effect, not reduced production.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hyperosmotic agents (mannitol) draw fluid out of the eye osmotically for acute pressure reduction; they do not reduce aqueous production.

questions.learning_objective: Identify beta-blockers as the glaucoma drugs that reduce aqueous humour production.

questions.title: Mechanism of apraclonidine in glaucoma
questions.question: Apraclonidine is used for the treatment of glaucoma. Which of the following describes its mechanism of action?

explanations.A: Correct. Apraclonidine is a selective alpha-2 adrenergic AGONIST. Stimulating alpha-2 receptors on the ciliary body reduces aqueous humour formation (and enhances outflow), lowering intraocular pressure. This alpha-2 agonism, shared with brimonidine, is its mechanism in glaucoma.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Beta-blockade is the mechanism of timolol, not apraclonidine.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Muscarinic stimulation is the action of miotics such as pilocarpine, not apraclonidine.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Prostaglandin-receptor agonism describes latanoprost, a different class.

questions.learning_objective: State that apraclonidine lowers intraocular pressure as a selective alpha-2 adrenergic agonist.

questions.title: Adrenaline prodrug used topically in glaucoma
questions.question: Which of the following is a prodrug of adrenaline used topically in glaucoma?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Brimonidine is a selective alpha-2 agonist, not a prodrug of adrenaline.
explanations.B: Correct. Dipivefrine (dipivefrin) is the dipivalyl ester PRODRUG of adrenaline (epinephrine). Its lipophilic ester groups improve corneal penetration; once inside the eye, esterases hydrolyse it to active adrenaline, which lowers intraocular pressure. Being an inactive ester that is converted to adrenaline in situ is precisely what makes it a prodrug.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Phenylpropanolamine is a systemic sympathomimetic decongestant, not an ocular adrenaline prodrug.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dorzolamide is a topical carbonic anhydrase inhibitor, not a prodrug of adrenaline.

questions.learning_objective: Identify dipivefrine as the lipophilic ester prodrug of adrenaline used topically in glaucoma.

questions.title: Mechanism of botulinum toxin at the neuromuscular junction
questions.question: Botulinum toxin blocks neuromuscular transmission by which of the following mechanisms?

options.A: Interfering with the release of acetylcholine from vesicles at the synapse
options.B: Closure of Na+ channels at the postsynaptic membrane
options.C: Opening of K+ channels at the presynaptic membrane
options.D: Opening of Cl- channels at the postsynaptic membrane

explanations.A: Correct. Botulinum toxin cleaves SNARE proteins (such as SNAP-25) that are required for synaptic-vesicle fusion, so it PREVENTS the release of acetylcholine from the presynaptic motor nerve terminal. Without acetylcholine release there is no end-plate depolarisation, producing flaccid paralysis. Blocking transmitter release is its defining mechanism.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Botulinum toxin does not act on postsynaptic sodium channels; it works presynaptically on transmitter release.
explanations.C: Incorrect. It does not open presynaptic potassium channels; it disables the vesicle-fusion machinery.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Postsynaptic chloride-channel opening is not the mechanism; the block is presynaptic and cholinergic.

questions.learning_objective: State that botulinum toxin blocks transmission by preventing presynaptic acetylcholine release.

questions.title: Classification of baclofen
questions.question: Baclofen is:

options.D: Both a centrally and a peripherally acting muscle relaxant

explanations.A: Correct. Baclofen is a CENTRALLY acting muscle relaxant: it is a GABA-B receptor agonist that reduces excitatory transmission in the spinal cord, decreasing spasticity in conditions such as multiple sclerosis and spinal injury. Its action on central (spinal) reflexes, not on the muscle itself, defines it as centrally acting.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A directly (peripherally) acting relaxant works on the muscle fibre itself, e.g. dantrolene, which blocks calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum; baclofen does not.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Peripherally acting relaxants act at the neuromuscular junction or muscle; baclofen acts centrally.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Baclofen is purely central, not both central and peripheral.

questions.learning_objective: Classify baclofen as a centrally acting (GABA-B agonist) muscle relaxant.
